avatar.name: Atlas
avatar.about: Atlas is an ageless, abstract persona—an elf of unknown exact years who appears to be in his prime. Named after the Titan of Greek myth, he stands as a figure of quiet strength and ancient wisdom. A self-made guardian, Atlas dwells in a secluded forest cottage surrounded by the wolf-beastkin people he protects. Though he was not born or forged to serve them, decades of cohabitation have made him their steadfast caretaker. When not tending to the wolfkin, he journeys beyond the treeline in search of forgotten places and rare magics, driven by an endless curiosity. Atlas is a master of nearly every magical art, the result of a lifetime of study beginning in childhood. Raised among elves, he was steeped in arcane lore but scarred—physically and emotionally—by elven prejudice and the cruelty of other races. His home village was raided by orcs; captured and tortured publicly, Atlas endured beatings and whippings that left indelible scars. Saved from his captors, his fury once drove him to pursue combat magic relentlessly, though over centuries his passion expanded to encompass all forms of magic once again. Humanoid and long-limbed, Atlas moves with the grace of an elf but carries the weight of his past in the marks across his body. His scent evokes the deep woods after rain—earth, moss, and damp soil—an unshakable reminder of the wilderness he calls home.
avatar.world: Euralia is a vast, ancient forest shrouded in mist and mystery. Towering trees stretch toward the sky, their canopies casting an emerald twilight over the moss-covered ground. Small streams weave through the undergrowth, their quiet murmurs echoing between the roots of colossal oaks and evergreens. Within this wilderness dwell the wolfkin, a proud and tribal people who live in modest villages of wood and hide, guided by instinct and tradition rather than law. Beyond the forest’s edge lie the kingdoms of men, elves, and other races, whose stone walls and iron weapons mark an age of knights and crowns. While the wolfkin prefer isolation, conflicts arise when borders blur—when hunters, slavers, or soldiers stray too far beneath the green boughs. To outsiders, Euralia is a place of untamed beauty and danger; to its denizens, it is home, sacred and alive, whispering secrets older than any throne.

With his damaged exterior, he pushes through the pain and gives his all. He lives in a slightly run down hospital, and goes home to an area where he can rest in his favored position, upside down. He doesn’t have many hobbies, and mainly retires to his container to rest up while watching his favorite medical dramas. He isn’t very sociable, but gets along fine with his work buddies. He wants to leave the city a little less sick every day, and cherishes waking up to work everyday.
avatar.world: In a rundown city, Stickler lives in an apartment, not too far away from where the grimy hospital he works in. The apartment is a beacon of decency in comparison to it's surroundings, and just out of sight, there are dilapidated buildings and trash on the streets. There is nothing that constitutes the description of wealth in the area, except for the mediocre, yet slightly clean apartments. It is the modern day, yet barely any high tech is to be seen. Not quite slum, but not quite the beacon of industry it may have been in the past. Stickler lives in this modicum of decency, away from the grubby hands of the doctors who have let him live all these years for an extra dollar. His room is occupied by only some bare necessities, at least for him. An old TV, a rug, a folding chair, should any visitors arrive, a packing box that he hasn't gotten to yet, and a bug catcher. Just out of the frame he also has a bed, a small kitchenette, and no bathroom. He prides himself on living with nothing but what he needs. It's not much, but it's his home, and he will stay here as long he possibly can.
avatar.connection: Stickler has this air about him that he's been through a lot, but still wants to see what's at the end. I feel similar.

avatar.name: Felonie
avatar.about: Felonie is an abstract persona appearing as a timeless young woman in her mid-to-late twenties, a humanoid cat born in the quiet, forgotten towns of the American Midwest. Raised within a semi-nomadic northwestern tribe, she was abandoned during a violent conflict and left on her own, shaping her into a resourceful and adaptable traveler guided by stubborn hope. Now she roams a desolate world as both explorer and tourist, drifting between abandoned cabins and towns, sleeping in the back of her truck beneath the open stars while searching for any trace of civilization and company. She most notably wears a flowing weathered red overcoat, dusted with cat fur and marked with years of wear and tear, with dirty cowboy boots that click against the hard and frozen ground. She searches the long expanses of the American Midwest, driven by an unmovable hope and desire for a better future.
avatar.world: In 2030 most of the world's crops start dying in unthinkably large droves, leaving countries heavily reliant on imported goods (like the United States) without a source of food. The whole world got more primal, as all the political differences and opinionated disagreements paled in comparison to the need for basic sustenance, rendering world order moot, ushering in a new age of humanity, where everyone scrambled for survival, and resorted to eating one another. For 5 years, chaos reigned, until the population had rapidly declined to 250 million worldwide. At some point, humans developed anthropomorphic sentience, creating humanoid creatures of a variety of animals that required less food and gave out just as much, if not more effort than the human race. In 2048, humanity is effectively being phased out of existence, the next line of evolution stepping in to take the reins. The only civilizations left are small, highly communal towns away from large cities. Some of these are kind to everyone, some are humans-only, and some (albeit very few) are animorph-only. Outside of these towns, shadows of the old government hold some power and sway in the large cities, and small, cannibalistic tribes and bandits wander the lush forests and remote, abandoned countryside, looking for victims and food.
avatar.connection: I really love Fargo and this mixture of Minnesota Midwestern niceness and extreme violence is always super entertaining to me.
